Prof. Santos Kumar Das

Abstract:

Free Space Optical (FSO) communication has attracted significant attention as a highcapacity wireless transmission technology. It offers advantages such as wide bandwidth, high data transmission capability, and operation without licensed spectrum. Because of these features, FSO systems are considered suitable for applications including wireless backhaul networks and satellite communication links. However, the performance of an FSO link is strongly affected by atmospheric conditions. Environmental factors such as turbulence, fog, and misalignment between the transmitter and receiver can introduce signal fading and attenuation, which reduce signal quality and overall link reliability. To address these challenges, this work presents a deep learning-based modulation classification framework for FSO communication systems using a CNN-LSTM architecture. The proposed model processes received in-phase and quadrature samples directly, removing the need for manual feature extraction. Convolutional layers learn spatial signal characteristics, while the LSTM layer captures temporal dependencies. Simulation results under turbulence and fog conditions show reliable identification of different modulation schemes across several signal-to-noise ratio levels.
